mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of economic regime.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase exceeding 0.1 percentage points above 4.1% signals labor market deterioration that reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered periods, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts and retail sales growth signal broad consumer demand contraction that reduces corporate revenue expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline in the last month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both series decline, or Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: During industrial production contractions, manufacturing sector weakness reduces corporate profit margins and future earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of INDPRO decline periods, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI inflation rate increase above 3.5% signals persistent inflation that triggers restrictive monetary policy, reducing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered periods, or Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained employment growth, measured by PAYEMS increases, signals strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of economic regime.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of PAYEMS increase periods, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent declines in real personal consumption (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) signal weakening consumer demand that reduces corporate revenue growth expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and HOUST both decline in the last month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both series decline, or Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production decline below 100 (index) signals manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate capacity utilization and future earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of INDPRO decline periods, or Rank IC falls below 0.02 over any 3-year window.
